q1_issues.issue: The passive is stored under a converse head with the undergoer kind first, so the active 'words make up sentences' would yield (MakeUp word sentence) and the two voices produce records with nothing in common, which the voice-invariance rule forbids.

The head folds the passive's preposition 'of' into the verb symbol, whereas the phrasal-verb rule lemmatizes 'made up' to verb + particle only (make_up), giving no licence for a third element in the head.

q2_gaps: passive relational generic — the kind-level relation form is specified only for active clauses and gives no rule for argument order or head naming when the clause is passive ('Ns are made up of Ms')
constitution / part-whole holding between two KINDS — PartOf is defined only over individuals (a component of an object) and group members
notes: The relational-generic route itself is right (bare plural on both sides, 0.9/0.9 per the kind-characterization convention); MakeUpOf is an open-class lexical relation taken from the clause's own predicate, so the defect is its form and argument order, not its licence.
